newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Tel H1 China traffic up five pct.
newsitem.headline: HK Tel H1 China traffic up five pct.

text.p: Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd said on Tuesday that revenue from international services grew 4.8 percent to HK$8.74 billion in the six months to September 30, with China traffic growing five percent.

Overall international traffic grew 11 percent and non-China traffic grew 17 percent, as China traffic continued to be affected by tight inflationary controls in the mainland, chief executive Linus Cheung told a news conference.

Increasing callback services particularly on North American routes reduced international revenues as the Hong Kong outgoing call charge was replaced by a lower incoming payment from the callback country, Cheung said.
With the increase of callbacks, competitors originated or teminated an average 15 percent of both-way international traffic in the first half, he said.

The growth of callback could be seen in the rising ratio of outgoing-to-incoming calls to one-to-seven now from one-to-four or five six months ago, deputy chief executive Norman Yuen said. The cost to Hongkong Telecom was hard to quantify but it paid some HK$300 million in fees to its three fixed network competitors for calls they originated or terminated, he noted.

But Cheung said the Hongkong Telecom was successfully working to diversify away from its dependence on International Direct Dial (IDD), which now formed about 55 percent of overall revenues compared to 63 percent three years ago.
Growth in non-IDD revenue was 15 percent in the first half, he noted.

Revenue from local telephone services grew eight percent over the previous year to HK$2.13 billion, and that from other telecom services grew 38 percent to HK$3.79 billion reflecting growth in new value-added and data services, he said.
Overall revenue grew 9.3 percent to HK$15.92 billion.
Hong Kong Telecom is 57 percent owned by Britain's Cable & Wireless.
